metadata.title: Claude Code, Plugin Settings.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether getting a Claude Code plugin's settings to survive between sessions is a thing you ask Claude to remember or a thing you write down, using the plugin-settings skill's own .claude/plugin-name.local.md pattern as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a settings file is read fresh every time, in a shape simple enough to parse.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the enabled field driving the quick-exit pattern: toggles reliably when flat, silently mis-parsed when the YAML gets complex)

beats.narration_text: Someone wants Claude Code to remember a plugin's settings between sessions. It won't — each session starts blank. The real question: how does Claude Code read those settings back? One file holds the answer.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How do I get Claude Code to remember my plugin's settings between sessions?', hesitates on 'remember', corrects to 'read', lands the real question

props.text:
How do I get Claude Code
to remember my plugin's
settings between sessions?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('remember' -> 'read') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Telling Claude, in conversation, to remember a setting doesn't survive a new session — start over, and it's gone. What persists is a file: .claude/plugin-name.local.md, sitting in the project root. Above the line, YAML frontmatter holds structured fields — enabled, mode, a retry count. Below it, a markdown body holds free text, read back later.

shot.new_visual_element: A conversation bubble scattering past a session-restart divider; beside it a file icon staying fixed; the file splits into a frontmatter block on top and a markdown body block below

production_viz.label: A file, not a memory
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a speech-bubble labelled 'remember' fades and scatters as a vertical divider line labelled 'new session' sweeps past it. Right: a file icon labelled '.local.md' stays fixed and solid through the same divider, unaffected. The file then splits horizontally: the top region fills with flat key: value lines labelled 'YAML frontmatter'; the bottom region fills with wrapped prose lines labelled 'markdown body'.

beats.narration_text: Three consumers read that same file. A hook is a bash script — it parses the frontmatter with sed. A command uses the Read tool, in Claude's own context. An agent references it directly in its instructions. Watch the anchor: one field, enabled, drives a quick exit — check the file, check enabled, and stop before doing anything else if it's false.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — three consumer icons pointing at one file, then enabled: true/false driving a hook through check-file, check-enabled, to run or exit 0

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — one field, quick exit
production_viz.mechanic: Three cards fade in around a central file icon: 'hook' (terminal glyph, 'bash, parses with sed'), 'command' (magnifying glass, 'Read tool'), 'agent' (a simple figure glyph, 'in its instructions') — each with an arrow into the file. THE ANCHOR. Cards fade; below, a file corner reading 'enabled: true' zooms in, feeding a check-sequence box: 'file exists?' -> 'enabled?' -> branching to 'run' (teal) or 'exit 0' (terracotta). Toggle the field to false: the path lights straight to exit 0. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Flip enabled again — false, true, false — and the hook obeys every time; a flat field like that is exactly what a bash sed extraction is built for. But hand it something else — a multiline value, a quoted colon, an indented block — and that same parser can silently mangle what it reads back. No error appears. The frontmatter just stops matching what's on the page.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — enabled toggling the hook correctly three times, then a complex YAML block passing through the same sed scan and coming out wrong, no error shown

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — reliable, then silently wrong
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 CHECK SEQUENCE RETURNS, identical, and answers correctly three times in a row as 'enabled' flips false/true/false — each marked teal 'correct'. Then a second frontmatter block appears, this one with a quoted, colon-bearing value and an indented sub-list. A magnifying glass sweeps across it line by line, mimicking sed; when it crosses the quoted colon and the indented block, the extracted value shown beside it visibly does not match the source text, and a small label reads 'no error — just wrong'.

beats.narration_text: A plugin's settings aren't something you ask Claude to remember — they're a file it reads back every time, in a shape simple enough to parse, or not parsed at all.

props.quote: A plugin's settings aren't something you ask Claude to remember — they're a file it reads back every time, in a shape simple enough to parse, or not parsed at all.
props.sparkLine: Read fresh, or not at all.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Add a settings file to my plugin that stores an enabled flag and a validation mode, and have a hook check it before running. Watch three things when Claude answers: does it place the file at .claude/plugin-name.local.md, not somewhere else? Does it use YAML frontmatter above a markdown body, instead of one flat format? And does the hook check whether the file exists, then check enabled, and exit zero before doing anything else if either check fails? Liam, in for Bear.
